answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can use single-use, non-transferable vouchers: a new identity needs k vouchers from k distinct admitted agents, and each issuer may vouch only a few times. A voucher burns on use, and if a vouched identity attacks, its issuers lose their own bond. Think of a summit gate whose velvet passes carry a unique delta stamp: none can be copied or resold. To field N fakes, an attacker must corrupt k*N separate honest issuers, since vouchers cannot be bought or reused. That cost scales with the honest population, so a majority costs more than any prize.
